<id>css_performance_optimization</id> CSS Performance Optimization in Firefox Identification and resolution of massive CPU and RAM drains caused by unoptimized CSS selectors and compositing in Firefox custom themes. UI Architecture
<tag>CSS</tag> <tag>Performance</tag> <tag>CPU</tag> <tag>RAM</tag> <tag>Gecko</tag>
CSS might seem like simple styling, but in a massive application like a web browser, poorly optimized CSS selectors can absolutely crush the CPU and drain RAM by forcing the layout engine (Gecko/Servo) to constantly recalculate millions of nodes.
Three major performance killers were identified and neutralized:
1. **The Universal Selector Annihilation (CRITICAL DRAIN):** - **Bad:** `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; }` - **Why:** Using the universal `*` selector across the entire browser chrome forces the CPU to traverse and evaluate this rule against every single node in the browser's UI tree on every layout change. - **Fix:** Replaced with targeted selectors: `.tab-throbber, .tab-loading-burst, .urlbar-input, .tab-background, .tabbrowser-tab`.
2. **Linear-Gradient Compositing:** - **Bad:** `background-image: linear-gradient(...), url("...") !important;` - **Why:** Applying a dynamic gradient layered over a large JPG image forces the GPU/CPU to re-rasterize and composite the toolbar graphics constantly. - **Fix:** Removed the dynamic gradient from the CSS. Pre-composite the image offline instead.
3. **The [selected] Attribute Churn (Border vs Outline):** - **Bad:** `border: 1px solid #00FFFF !important;` - **Why:** Changing borders dynamically alters the element's box model dimensions, triggering a "layout thrash" rather than a simple repaint. - **Fix:** Swapped `border` for `outline`, which sits outside the box model and does not trigger reflows.
